key_insight: The paper shows that deep generative models with piecewise-affine decoders and Gaussian mixture priors can be identified unsupervised by breaking symmetry through algebraic contrast conditions.
engineering_relevance: This gives a principled route to recovering latent variables and decoder structure in nonlinear generative models, even when decoders are discontinuous or non-injective.
method: Domain contrast: removes global mixture symmetries in the latent prior.
Mechanism contrast: assigns each decoder branch a unique boundary witness.
Interaction contrast: prevents hidden parameter conspiracies between latent components and branches.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical identifiability hierarchy—law, map, posterior, and pointwise identifiability—derived from assumptions on the data-generating process rather than learning algorithms.
watch_item: The strongest identifiability guarantees still depend on specific symmetry-breaking assumptions, especially interaction contrast, so violations may limit practical applicability.
paper_title: Beyond ICA: Identifiability by Symmetry Breaking
